newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway aluminium makers pledge to reduce emissions.
newsitem.headline: Norway aluminium makers pledge to reduce emissions.

text.p: Norway's aluminium industry will reduce emissions of so-called greenhouse gases by 55 percent by 2005 under an agreement signed on Monday between producers and the Ministry of the Environment.

The agreement was inked by Norway's three producers of aluminium -- Elkem ASA, Hydro Aluminium, a division of industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA, and Soer-Norge Aluminium, a venture between Norsk Hydro and Alusuisse Lonza of Switzerland.
The three companies produced a combined 865,000 tonnes of primary aluminium in 1996.

The agreement details a reduction in emissions of 2.2 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, based on 1990 figures. The total accounts for about four percent of total Norwegian emissions of greenhouse gases.

The ministry said emissions from the aluminium industry were about 35 percent lower in 1995 than in 1990, meaning that industry had already reduced emissions by around 1.7 million tonnes per year, leaving just 500,000 tonnes to be cut between now and 2005.
Ola Boesterud, spokesman at Elkem, said the agreement would not have any impact on production.
"It will mean some additional investment but we're already a long way forward in reaching the goal," Boesterud told Reuters.
